correctness.rationale: Retaining each letter's first and last positions preserves singletons, diagonal pairs, and every distinct pair ab because ab is present exactly when first(a)<last(b). The resulting word has length at most 2q, with equality in the minimum precisely when all aa are present. Minimum representatives then have exactly two occurrences per letter; arbitrary representatives need only have at least two. Among these classes the only variable observations are ordered pairs of distinct letters, with ab missing exactly when last(b)<first(a). This identifies the observation set with the reversed complement of the strict interval order on distinct letters and proves both injectivity and reversal of inclusion. For surjectivity the strict predecessor sets in a (2+2)-free poset are nested: incomparable sets would supply a predecessor of each upper vertex missing below the other, giving an induced (2+2). For an element x let i be its predecessor-set index and j the first index of a set containing x, or one past the end. Then j>i and the interval [2i,2j−1] has the right strict comparisons; perturb ties within endpoint type without crossing an endpoint of the other type and read the endpoints in order. This yields the desired doubled word. Renaming commutes with the bijection; q=1 yields one deepest class, represented by aa. The independent endpoint enumeration gives 1,3,19,207,3451 signature/order classes through q=5; replay: python3 /workspace/branches/44766552-aa02-4b69-ae48-315dc237b573/independent_endpoint_check.py. This is not a reproduction of the frozen verifier's all-signature traversal. The denominators 152 and 2326 are from Table B.1 of arXiv:1310.1278; the labelled Brightwell–Keller asymptotic on p. 2 has 12√3/π^(5/2), (q!)²√q, exponential base 6/π² and relative error O(1/q), as stated.
